conceptual assets.concept: FIFO stored data (contents held in the FIFO memory or single-word register)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The RTL implements clocked storage and readout of user data: write processes perform indexed stores conditioned on the effective write enable (examples: "if (we = '1') then fifo_mem(to_integer(unsigned(w_pnt(...)))) <= wdata_i;" or for depth=1 "if (we = '1') then fifo_reg <= wdata_i;"), and read paths drive rdata_o from fifo_mem or fifo_reg (rdata_o <= fifo_mem(... ) in async/sync branches; rdata_o <= fifo_reg for depth=1). Reads and subsequent logic depend on the stored values, so the integrity of the stored FIFO contents is required for correct readout.

conceptual assets.concept: Effective write-enable decision that determines whether a write is performed
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes an effective write permission and uses it to perform writes and advance the write pointer: "we <= we_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (we_i and free);"; write processes and pointer update use that signal (writes occur only when we='1' and w_nxt increments when we='1'). Corruption of this decision changes whether data is recorded, so its integrity is required for correct write behavior.

conceptual assets.concept: Effective read-enable/consume decision that determines whether a read/consume occurs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes an effective read permission and uses it to advance the read pointer and enable read-side behavior: "re <= re_i when (FIFO_SAFE = false) else (re_i and avail);"; r_nxt increments when re='1' and read indexing uses r_pnt or r_pnt_ff. Corruption of this decision changes whether stored entries are consumed and read out, so its integrity is required for correct read/consume behavior.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO pointer state (write and read pointers that index storage and determine occupancy)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The write and read pointers are stored in the clocked pointer_reg process and determine where writes and reads occur and how status is computed: on reset the pointers are cleared ("if (rstn_i = '0') then w_pnt <= (others => '0'); r_pnt <= (others => '0');"), on clock edges they are updated ("elsif rising_edge(clk_i) then w_pnt <= w_nxt; r_pnt <= r_nxt;"). A registered copy r_pnt_ff is produced by async_r_pnt_reg for asynchronous reads. These pointers index fifo_mem/fifo_reg for writes/reads and feed full/empty/level calculations; their integrity is therefore required for correct addressing and status.

conceptual assets.concept: FIFO occupancy and status flags (level, full, empty, free, avail, half) as computed internally and reported on outputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: Occupancy and status are computed from the pointers and exported to ports; these flags also gate behavior when FIFO_SAFE is enabled. Examples: "match <= '1' when (r_pnt(...)=w_pnt(...)) else '0'"; "full <= '1' when (...) and (match = '1') else '0'"; "empty <= '1' when (...) and (match = '1') else '0'"; "level <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(w_pnt) - unsigned(r_pnt));"; "half <= level(level'left-1) or full;"; "free <= not full; avail <= not empty;". The outputs reflect these signals either combinationally (not FIFO_RSYNC) or via sync_status process (FIFO_RSYNC). Because writes/reads can be gated by free/avail and external observers use free_o/avail_o/half_o/level_o, the integrity of these computed status values is required for correct gating and reporting.
